title: Generic trivialization of a finite-coefficient sheaf by a finite normal cover
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian excellent integral scheme [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-pc-integral-scheme], let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, and let $F$ be a constructible sheaf of $A_X$-modules on the ordinary small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. There exist a finite surjective morphism $f:Y\to X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], a nonempty open subscheme $U\subseteq X$, and a finite $A$-module $N$ such that $Y$ is integral and normal (its local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]), $f^{-1}U\to U$ is finite etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $(f^*F)|_{f^{-1}U}\cong\underline N_{f^{-1}U}$ as sheaves of $A$-modules. Here $f^*$ is ordinary inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and $\underline N$ is the constant module sheaf. No finite-type hypothesis over a field is imposed.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 3.5.7, printed p.276 (the finite surjective normal integral cover and dense etale open). Algebraic and monodromy inputs: Stacks etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0DV5, label lemma-locally-constant-on-connected (3); morphisms.tex Tag 0AVK, label lemma-nagata-normalization-finite-general.

proof.text: Choose the stratum containing the generic point $\eta$ of $X$ in a constructible stratification for $F$. A locally closed subset containing $\eta$ is open: writing it as $V\cap C$ with $V$ open and $C$ closed, the inclusion $\eta\in C$ forces $C=X$. Thus its image is a nonempty open $U_0$. Replace its immersion by the open immersion of $U_0$, using immersion independence (both have the same image). Consequently $F|_{U_0}$ is locally constant with finite module values. This is the dense lisse open asserted in the source.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 3.5.7, printed p.276; explicit elaboration of the finite normal trivializing cover; Stacks 095E (lemma-constructible-quasi-compact-quasi-separated), 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant)

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq U_0$. Its ring $R$ is an excellent domain. By J-2 in the definition of excellence, applied to the identity finite-type $R$-algebra, the set of primes with regular local ring is open. It contains $(0)$: the local ring there is the function field and a field is regular. Take a principal open $U=D(a)$ containing $(0)$ inside this locus. Every local ring of $U$ is regular, so $U$ is normal by regular-implies-normal. It is nonempty, affine, integral and hence connected. Restricting the finite constant models from step 1 shows that $F|_U$ remains finite locally constant. This auxiliary shrinking uses excellence without imposing any finite-type-over-a-field hypothesis.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 3.5.7, printed p.276; explicit elaboration of the finite normal trivializing cover; Stacks 07QT (definition-excellent), J-2; 0567 (lemma-regular-normal)

proof.text: Forget the module structure of $F|_U$ and apply the finite-set monodromy torsor lemma. It gives a connected finite etale torsor $c:P\to U$ on which the underlying sheaf becomes constant. A torsor has a nonempty fibre at every geometric point, hence $c$ is surjective and $P$ is nonempty. Apply module-constant-of-set-pullback to obtain $c^*(F|_U)\cong\underline N_P$ as $A$-module sheaves. The module $N$ is finite: choose a geometric point of $P$; its stalk is $N$ by the constant-stalk lemma and also a stalk of $F|_U$ by inverse-image stalk comparison and forgetful compatibility. That latter stalk is finite by the finite-values lemma. The comparison isomorphisms for abelian inverse image suffice to check finiteness of the underlying set.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 3.5.7, printed p.276; explicit elaboration of the finite normal trivializing cover; Stacks 0DV5 (lemma-locally-constant-on-connected), parts (1) and (3); 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback)

proof.text: Because $U$ is affine and $c$ finite, write $P=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ finite over $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. The finite-algebra Noetherian lemma gives that $P$ is Noetherian. Etale normal components over the normal integral scheme $U$ now decompose $P$ into finitely many open-and-closed normal integral schemes. Connectedness and nonemptiness of $P$ force exactly one component, so $P$ is normal integral. Put $K=k(X)=k(U)$ and $L=k(P)$. The generic point of $P$ maps to the generic point of $U$: the image of its closure contains the image of $P$, which is all of $U$. On the affine map $P\to U$, the etale residue-field lemma at the generic point therefore gives that $L/K$ is finite separable.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 3.5.7, printed p.276; explicit elaboration of the finite normal trivializing cover; Stacks 033C (lemma-normal-goes-up), 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field)

proof.text: The scheme $X$ is quasi-separated since it is Noetherian. Normalize $X$ in $L$ using normalization in a finite residue-field extension at its generic point. This gives $f:Y\to X$, with $Y$ integral normal and generic field $L$. It is finite: on any nonempty affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$, its ring is the integral closure of the excellent domain $R$ in $L$, by the affine normalization construction. The ring $R$ is quasi-excellent, hence Nagata; taking the prime $(0)$ in the definition of Nagata makes $R$ Japanese. Since $L/k(X)$ is finite, the definition of Japanese says precisely that this integral closure is a finite $R$-module. Thus the definition of a finite morphism applies on every affine. Finally a finite morphism is proper and hence closed; its image contains $\eta$, so its closed image is all of $X$. Thus $f$ is surjective.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 3.5.7, printed p.276; explicit elaboration of the finite normal trivializing cover; Stacks 01OY; 035H (definition-normalization-X-in-Y), 035L (lemma-normal-normalization), 07QV (lemma-quasi-excellent-nagata), 032R (definition-nagata), 032F (definition-N)

proof.text: Over the affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of step 2, write again $P=\operatorname{Spec}B$. We check directly that $B$ is the integral closure of $R$ in $L$. First $B$ lies in that closure, since it is finite over $R$ and finite algebras are integral. Conversely, an element $z\in L$ integral over $R$ is integral over every local ring $\mathcal O_{P,p}$ (the same monic polynomial has coefficients there). Those local rings are integrally closed in their common fraction field $L$, by normality of $P$ and the integral-scheme stalk/function-field lemma. Thus $z$ lies in every $\mathcal O_{P,p}$; the function-field sections-glue lemma yields $z\in\Gamma(P,\mathcal O_P)=B$. The affine description of normalization therefore identifies $f^{-1}U=\operatorname{Spec}B=P$ over $U$, with the same structure map $c$. In particular $f^{-1}U\to U$ is finite etale.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 3.5.7, printed p.276; explicit elaboration of the finite normal trivializing cover; Stacks 0358 (lemma-normal-integral-sections), the same local monic-polynomial argument; affine normalization construction

proof.text: Under the isomorphism of step 6, the composite $P\to Y\to X$ equals $P\xrightarrow c U\hookrightarrow X$. The inverse-image composition isomorphisms identify $(f^*F)|_{f^{-1}U}$ with $c^*(F|_U)$, hence with $\underline N_P$ from step 3. The composition isomorphisms on underlying abelian sheaves are natural in all endomorphisms of $F$, so commute with multiplication by each $a\in A$; they are therefore $A$-linear. This gives the asserted module-sheaf isomorphism. Steps 2, 3, 5 and 6 give the required nonempty $U$, finite $N$, integral normal $Y$, finite surjective $f$, and finite etale restriction.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N8-28780ee5b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 7 steps and all 34 cited statements in full, plus ILO XVII Lemma 3.5.7 at printed p.276 (PDF p.282). The source asserts the finite surjective normal integral cover with a dense finite étale open on which M becomes constant, using the word 'évidemment'. The item states this claim in more generality (Noetherian excellent integral X, any finite ring A). That is true and the statement is unchanged; there are no new nodes. Step checks: (1) the stratum containing η is open because η lies in the closed factor, and immersion independence moves it to the open immersion. (2) J-2 applied with A=R makes the regular locus open; (0) is in it because O_{X,η} is a field and fields are regular; so D(a) is normal by rem-pc-regular-normal (1) and connected. (3) The set monodromy torsor's fibres are nonempty by def-sbc, so P is nonempty and c surjective; module-constant-of-set-pullback gives N; N is finite via the constant-sheaf stalk, inverse-image stalk-germ, forget-naturality and module-values (2). (4) B is Noetherian, etale-normal-components plus connectedness gives one component, generic maps to generic, and the étale residue-field lemma gives L/K finite separable. (5) X is quasi-separated, normalization in L exists; R is quasi-excellent, hence Nagata, hence N-2, so the normalization is finite; finite ⇒ proper ⇒ closed image containing η ⇒ surjective. (6) Both inclusions B ⊆ closure ⊆ B hold via finite⇒integral, stalks-in-function-field and sections-glue, so f^{-1}U ≅ P over U. (7) Inverse-image composition plus forget-naturality, made A-linear by naturality. Edge cases checked: Spec K, F=0, A=0, constant F, non-normal X. I found no duplicate (perfect-closure-finite-normal-model and generic-curve-model are narrower) and no cycle. I accept the 21 declared tool_uses: all are generic algebra or étale-sheaf black boxes. No SGA is cited, and no fixes were needed.
